[Cockroach Janta Party] The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP; lit. 'Cockroach People's Party') is a political movement founded on 16 May 2026 by political communications strategist and activist Abhijeet Dipke. The CJP harnessed widespread political and economic discontent among Generation Z in India, leading to protests in Delhi and other cities. The "party" was created in response to remarks made on 15 May 2026 by Surya Kant, the Chief Justice of India, who allegedly referred to certain activists and unemployed youth as "cockroaches" and "parasites of society". Kant later clarified that he was referring specifically to people with fraudulent degrees, but the remarks drew criticism amid concerns about the economic and political prospects of young people. The movement's name parodies India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The party gained a large social-media following soon after its formation. Its five-point manifesto addressed parliamentary conduct, election commissioners, women's political representation and media licensing. Beginning in June, the CJP led nationwide protests over medical entrance examination irregularities, which ended after talks with the government and Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation on 25 July 2026. It later joined protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral-roll irregularities. In October 2026, CJP leaders were released from custody after undertaking not to call protests at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi.
